data.name: Briseida
data.gender_notes: Briseida is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek brēsis (fair-haired) and eidos (appearance or form). The name Briseida carries the meaning “Fair-haired” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Briseida usually hope their child will grow to embody fair-haired and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Representing the inner beauty of a soul.
data.etymology: Briseida belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fair-haired.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Briseida total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: בְּרִישֵׂדָע
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שֵׁם זֶה יָצוּעַ מִן-הַיְּהוּדִי, וְכוֹכבָה שִׁיר. מֵקָרֶב הַמִּקְרָא, וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי, וְהָאֱגָר. בְּרִישֵׂדָע, דָּע, 'בנו של פְּרִיזָה', הוּא, 'זֶה, אוֹ, הַיּ, נָשִׂיא, לְבַת, פְּרִיזָה, הָאֱגָרִית'.

in_greek.name: Βρισηδᾶ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ ὄνομα Βρισηδᾶ, ἔχει τὴν ἐτυμολογίαν ἀπὸ τῆς ἑβραϊκῆς λέξεως, Βְּרִישֵׂדָע. Ἔχει τὴν σημασίαν ὕπερμαχος. Ἐν τῇ ἔμφασῐ̑ τῆς ἑβραϊκῆς γλώσσης, ὁ Βρισηδᾶ, καλοῦται ὁ ὑπὲρμαχος, τὸν ὑπὲρ τοὺς ἄλλους. Ἐν τῇ ἔμφασῐ̑ τῆς Χριστιανικῆς ἐκκλησιᾶς, ὁ Βρισηδᾶ, καλοῦται ὁ ὑπὲρμαχος, τὸν ὑπὲρ τοὺς ἄλλους.

in_latin.name: Briseida
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Briseida, ex Hebraico, Βְּרִישֵׂדָע, derivatur. Significat felicitas fortitudo. In ambitu Hebraico, Briseida, Felix Fortis, nominatur. In ambitu Ecclesiae Christianae, Briseida, Felix Fortis, nominatur.

in_english.name: Briseida
in_english.meaning: Name of a woman, meaning 'Felix Fortis', or 'Fortunate and Strong'
in_english.long_meaning: The name Briseida is derived from the Hebrew name, Βְּרִישֵׂדָע, which means 'Felix Fortis', or 'Fortunate and Strong'. In the Hebrew context, Briseida refers to a woman of great fortune and strength. In the Christian tradition, Briseida is associated with qualities of fortitude and resilience, and is often given to children born into strong and loving families.

data.cultural_impact: The name Briseida, derived from the Greek words brēsis (fair-haired) and eidos (appearance or form), has ancient roots and signifies a striking or beautiful appearance. This name has been cherished through history, particularly in literature, where the character Briseis appears in Homer's Iliad, famed for her beauty. This name potentially carries the cultural weight of not only physical beauty but also the sophistication and depth of ancient Greek heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Briseida, beyond its tangible meaning of fair-haired and beautiful appearance, also holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the inner radiance and divine aspects within each person. This name could be considered a call to embrace one's unique inner beauty, wisdom, and worthiness as a child of the divine. A name that encourages self-love, confidence, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Briseis in Greek mythology was a Trojan princess known for her beauty and strength, captured by Achilles. In Christian tradition, Briseida represents the soul's inner turmoil and vulnerability, symbolizing the human capacity for both strength and weakness in the face of trials and temptations.

historical_references.reference: Briseida was a Trojan princess who fell in love with Menelaus, the husband of Helen of Troy, during the siege of Troy.

trends: as a given name for girls
modern_usage.modern_context: Briseida is a name of Greek origin that has gained popularity as a given name for girls in the modern era. It is derived from the Greek word 'briseis,' which means 'carrying a burden' or 'taken away.' In mythology, Briseida was a Trojan princess who fell in love with Menelaus during the siege of Troy. Today, the name is often associated with strength, beauty, and grace.

name_in_real_life.story: Sarah Briseida from Athens, Greece embodies the meaning of Briseida - "Fair-haired". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
